studies.Population: Men in the population-based Cancer of the Prostate in Sweden study, including incident prostate cancer cases and population controls.
studies.Ethnicity Basis: NA: no field-specific ethnicity evidence was available
studies.Reference: Total antioxidant intake and prostate cancer in the Cancer of the Prostate in Sweden (CAPS) study. A case control study.
studies.Authors: Russnes KM, Möller E, Wilson KM, Carlsen M, Blomhoff R, Smeland S, Adami HO, Grönberg H, Mucci LA, Bälter K
studies.Timing: Diet was assessed after diagnosis; the questionnaire was sent an average of 5 months after diagnosis.
studies.comparison_type: More than 1–3 chocolate servings per month versus no chocolate consumption

sample_size.location: Results, Table 4, Chocolate section; total_n derived from reported group counts 1112 + 1489 = 2601

effect_size.excerpt: For chocolate intake, there was a positive association with total, advanced, localized and low grade prostate cancer (total OR = 1.43, 95 % CI 1.12–1.82, advanced 1.40, 95 % CI 1.01–1.96, localized 1.43, 95 % CI 1.08–1.88, and low grade 1.41, 95 % CI 1.03–1.93).

confidence_interval.excerpt: For chocolate intake, there was a positive association with total, advanced, localized and low grade prostate cancer (total OR = 1.43, 95 % CI 1.12–1.82, advanced 1.40, 95 % CI 1.01–1.96, localized 1.43, 95 % CI 1.08–1.88, and low grade 1.41, 95 % CI 1.03–1.93).

timing.excerpt: Average time between date of diagnosis and date when the questionnaire was sent was 5 months.
